 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the death of L.Kumaraswamy S/o Late Reddappa in a Road Traffic Accident.
The petitioners are the mother and sister of deceased L.Kumaraswamy.

2. The Petition averments are as under:
That on 15.09.2019 at about 4.00 p.m., on Punganur- Chowdepalli Road, near Chadala Bus-stop, Punganur Mandal, Chittoor District, while L.Kumaraswamy was proceeding on the Splendor Motor-cycle bearing no.AP-03-AJ-7738 along with one Sivaraj as pillion, a Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01-AC-6922 driven by its driver at high-speed in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed against the Motor-cycle.
As a result, Kumaraswamy fell-down and sustained grievous-injuries.

He was immediately shifted to Community Health Centre,
Punganur, where he succumbed to the injuries.

Prior to the date of accident,
L.Kumaraswamy was hale and healthy and was a Mechanic earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
3. That the accident was solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Container Lorry.
Respondent no.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said lorry, and are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
4. After the service of notice, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsel and filed their objections to the main petition.

5. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.1-Owner has stated that the offending Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01-AC-6922 was insured with respondent no.2 and the insurance was in force as on the date of accident.
It is also stated that the driver of the said Lorry had valid Driving Licence as on the date of accident.

Thus, if at all the compensation is awarded, respondent no.2-Insurer is A. Reddamma vs Cool Hub Logistics on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148408301/
2 liable to pay the same.

sentences.text:
Thus, it is prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
6.
In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.2-Insurance Company has admitted the issuance of Policy in respect of Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01-AC-6922.
However the age, avocation and income of the deceased is denied.

It is the specific contention of respondent no.2 that since the Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01- AC-6922 is not at all involved in the accident, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of lorry; that the accident is due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
Further, that the owner of the insured lorry has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

That the driver of the lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and that the insured has willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person having no driving licence.
On these grounds, Respondent no.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

[
7. On the rival pleadings, the following Issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that they are the legal representatives of the deceased?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that L.Kumaraswamy S/o Late Reddappa died due to injuries sustained by him in an accident occurred on 15-09-2019 at about 4.00 p.m., on Punganoor-Chowdepalli road, near Chadalla bus stop, Punganur, Chittor district, A.P, arising due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Container lorry bearing Reg. No.NL-01-AC-6922?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?
8. On behalf of petitioners, petitioner no.1 has been examined as P.W.1 and got marked 25 documents as per Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-25; an eyewitness has been as PW.2 and Ex.P.26 has been marked.

On the other hand, Respondent no.2 has examined two witnesses as RWs.1 & 2 and have got marked Exs.R.1 to 6.

12. Issue No.2:-

It is the case of the Petitioners that one L.Kumaraswamy who is the son of petitioner no.1 and brother of petitioner no.2, has died in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the driver of the offending Container lorry bearing No.NL-01-AC-6922.
13.

On the other hand, Respondent no.1-Owner has stated that the offending Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01-AC-6922 was insured with respondent no.2 and the insurance was in force as on the date of accident.
It is also stated that the driver of the said Lorry had valid Driving Licence as on the date of accident.
Thus if at all the compensation is awarded, respondent no.2-Insurer is liable to pay the same.

Whereas, Respondent no.2-Insurance Company has denied the involvement of the Container Lorry bearing no.NL-01-AC- 6922, and that the accident was due to the rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the said lorry.
